t: Find the Largest Palindrome Divisible by K
o: A palindrome is fully determined by its first half, so we search over halves greedily: build the left half digit by digit from 9 downward, and at each step check whether the remaining free digits can still complete a value ≡ 0 (mod k). Feasibility is answered by a backward DP over residues: g[i][r] = can free positions i..h−1 achieve residual r. Since k ≤ 9, each DP layer is a 10-element boolean array, and the whole construction is O(n·k·10).
k: Digit i and its mirror n−1−i carry combined weight (10^(n−1−i) + 10^i) mod k (or just 10^i for the exact middle).
Backward DP g[i] = set of residues achievable by choosing digits for free positions i..h−1 enables an O(k) feasibility test per candidate digit.
Greedy from the most significant digit down with the largest feasible digit yields the maximum palindrome.

a.n: Approach 1: Backward residue DP + greedy reconstruction
a.i: Precompute g layers once; then walk positions choosing the biggest digit whose residue keeps (needed − d·w_i) inside g[i+1]. Existence is guaranteed because some n-digit k-palindrome exists (e.g., repunit-based constructions for each k ≤ 9).
s: h = (n+1)//2; compute pow10 mod k; weight w_i = (pow10[n−1−i] + pow10[i]) % k (halve for the middle when i == n−1−i).
g[h] = {0}; for i from h−1 down: g[i][r] = OR over d in 0..9 of g[i+1][(r − d·w_i) mod k].
Reconstruct: need = 0; for i in 0..h−1: for d from (i==0 ? 1 : 9) down to 0: if g[i+1][(need − d·w_i) mod k] exists, take d, need = (need − d·w_i) mod k.
Mirror the chosen half to form the answer string.
a.t: O(n·k·10) — building the DP layers and reconstructing, each position tries ≤10 digits against a k-sized layer
a.sp: O(n·k) for the DP layers and power table

a.n: Approach 2: Forward greedy with recomputed feasibility (conceptual)
a.i: At each position, tentatively place the largest digit and run a fresh reachability DP for the remaining positions. Correct but O(h²·k·10) — too slow for n = 1e5; included to motivate the precomputed backward DP.
s: Fix prefix progressively; for each candidate digit, run the suffix reachability DP from scratch.
Accept the largest digit that admits completion.
a.t: O(n·k·10) as implemented (the naive recompute-per-digit variant would be O(h²·k·10) and is infeasible at n = 1e5)

w: Key checks: n = 1 (single digit, must be a positive multiple of k, e.g. n=1,k=4 → "8"), odd/even mirroring offsets, and the leading digit never being 0. The backward-DP-over-residues pattern generalizes to 'largest string satisfying a modular constraint'. Verify example 3: n=5,k=6 → "89898" (89898 = 6·14983).
